name: Predictive Coding Active Learning Evaluation
description: Active learning is a popular methodology in text classification - known in the legal domain as "predictive coding" or "Technology Assisted Review" or "TAR" - due to its potential to minimize the required review effort to build effective classifiers. In this study, we use extensive experimentation to examine the impact of popular seed set selection strategies in active learning, within a predictive coding exercise, and evaluate different active learning strategies against well-researched continuous active learning strategies for the purpose of determining efficient training methods for classifying large populations quickly and precisely. We study how random sampling, keyword models and clustering based seed set selection strategies combined together with top-ranked, uncertain, random, recall inspired, and hybrid active learning document selection strategies affect the performance of active learning for predictive coding. We use the percentage of documents requiring review to reach 75% r
general_score_metric: review effort to reach target recall
reputation: A specialized evaluation setup in legal text classification and predictive coding research, with limited adoption outside information retrieval and e-discovery studies.
notes: Benchmarking is tied to active learning protocol choices, so results are not directly comparable across studies; not an LLM benchmark and depends heavily on dataset and stopping criteria.
